title.zh: 卷36 志十一 天文十一 五星合聚
title.en: Volume 36 Treatises 11: Astronomy 11, Conjunctions of the Five Planets
title.raw: 卷36 志十一 天文十一 五星合聚

sentences.zh: 五星合聚

translations.literal: Conjunctions and Gatherings of the Five Planets.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunctions of the Five Planets.

sentences.zh: 天官書言同舍為合，於兩星、三星、四星、五星之合各有占，而以五星合為最吉，謂經度之同如合朔也。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Celestial Offices states that sharing a lodge constitutes conjunction; for conjunctions of two, three, four, or five stars there are respective prognostications, but the conjunction of all five planets is regarded as most auspicious, meaning that their ecliptic longitudes coincide as at new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Celestial Offices holds that stars sharing a lodge are in conjunction; pairings, triplets, quadruplets, and full pentads each carry their own omens, yet the alignment of all five planets is deemed most auspicious—when their longitudes meet as at new moon.

sentences.zh: 茲就三星以上同宮同宿，及兩星以上同度者，著於篇。

translations.literal: Herein are recorded in this chapter those cases of three or more stars sharing palace and lodge, and of two or more stars at the same degree.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter sets down cases in which three or more planets shared a palace and lodge, and those in which two or more shared the same degree.
